inShort: For two-handed backhands: B takes the paddle hand off and hits off-hand forehands, to feel the hand that shapes the stroke.
rules: B stands at the baseline. A stands at the kitchen line across the net and feeds calm balls to B's backhand side.
B takes the paddle hand off and swings with the off hand alone, like a forehand with that hand. This hand guides the paddle and puts the spin on the ball.
On the take-back, point the paddle face toward the back fence, not flat down.
Brush up the back of the ball from below, swing through and forward, and finish like a windshield wiper.
After 10–15 balls, put the paddle hand back on and keep the same brush.
tooEasy: With both hands back on, 7 of 10 drives land cross-court behind A's kitchen. Even harder: A varies the height, from knee to shoulder.
tooHard: A feeds slow, easy balls, and nobody counts.
goodLooksLike: The ball leaves with topspin and dips into the court, and the paddle turns over out in front like a windshield wiper.
